questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Going to a English-speaking country. To improven my written as well as my oral English.

Furtherly, I wanted to travel to a vibrant city with a vast varities of activities as a student and local. On top of that, the choice of Bristol was an opt-out of London. I wanted to travel to a city with locals, and a size that is managable.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The service-level was 10. The teaching was an overall 10. The location was an overall 10.

My rate of 3 is all in all centered around my specific semester, where the teachers were a part of the Industrial Strike. 
I sympathized with the teachers' strike, but it had negative consequences of my experience, where 7 out of 13 teaching weeks was canceled.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The Global Opportunities office in Bristol was very informative up to the arrival, during the stary and afterwards. Further, The Global Opportunities office was also a hotspot for International Students in Global Lounge, and arranged many activities for the international students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Advice for accomodation, visa rules, how to apply for classes etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. Bristol's housings is old, expensive and unmanagable.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That the busses are unreliant. There are many opportunities for electric scooters, and many international biked as well. I was lucky to live near campus and walked to everything.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: What I understood, it is difficult for University of Bristol to offer accomodation for postgraduates. Nearly all of the international's was offered student accomodation by the university.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had to write to the university a couple of times, but the university was really helpful.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After I got accepted I was emailed a list of available classes. I then chose three. Even after arrival I had the opportunity to switch classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Global Opportunities and Study Programme's Study Office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choosing the classes you like.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The degree of difficulty was tmanagable. In terms of the assesments, there is not an essay culture at my home university. But the teachers took the time to give me feedback and assist my writing process.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More critical discussions teachers and students in between and less structured teacher-advised classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Politics of Brexit
Politics of (Un)Sustainability
Care, Labour and Gender

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Don't remember others. I was really happy about my choices though.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I were a part of the Running Society and Spikeball society.

The University have plenty of choices and opportunities: Even a bubble tea society if you like drinking that.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think there is +400 societies and clubs. So whatever you like.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Bath for sure. Stonehenge is close by and Salisbury to see the Magna Carta.

Cornwall and Devon and just go to the coast. 

Wales is 30 min away by train and Cardiff 55 min.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Societies and clubs!!!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Don't know

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness by everyone! British people are very polite

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Expect to use a lot on housing, and that the condition of the housings are poor
2. That Bristol is an amazing city!
3. Good academic culture

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in another country is a gift

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't know

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
